newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian reform commission meets, D'Alema chairman.
newsitem.headline: Italian reform commission meets, D'Alema chairman.

text.p: A special commission of parliament set up to draft reforms to Italy's constitution elected the leader of the country's biggest party, Massimo D'Alema of the Democratic Party of the Left, as its chairman on Wednesday.

The 70-member commission, which was meeting for the first time, has until the end of June to recommend changes to give Italy stable government, establish a new parliamentary structure and decentralise the state.

D'Alema, whose ex-communist PDS is the biggest in parliament and the centre-left government, was elected chairman with 52 votes. His only rival, Rolando Fontan of the separatist Northern League, won six votes and 12 ballots were blank, officials said.
The commission includes members of all parties in parliament and is formed equally from the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) and the Senate (upper house).
D'Alema is one of several party leaders on the commission. Centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi and his hard-right ally Gianfranco Fini are also members.

Constitutional reform is the most difficult political task confronting Italy, which has had more than 50 governments since World War Two. Deep differences divide the parties on the best blueprint for stability.
